newsitem.title: USA: Cavalier sees deal slightly dilutive.
newsitem.headline: Cavalier sees deal slightly dilutive.

text.p: Cavalier Homes Inc said its planned $77.4 million purchase of Belmont Homes Inc is expected to dilute earnings slightly in 1997 and 1998.

The stock transaction announced earlier has a fixed ratio and a price protection mechanism - or "collar" - that allows Belmont to walk away from the deal if the Cavalier stock price falls more than 25 percent, officials of both companies said in a telephone conference call.
Under the plan, each share of Belmont would fetch 0.80 share of Cavalier. Based on Wednesday's closing prices, the deal valued Belmont at about $8.15 per share.

Cavalier chief executive David Roberson said the transaction was expected to give the mobile home makers a stronger position in the competitive industry that has been suffering from weak pricing and high retail inventories.
"This deal is not based on cost-cutting strategies or the loss of management or personnel," he said.
He also expressed hope that the industry's troubles would be a short-term phenomenon.

"We do not feel like there is a fundamnetal problem with the ability for the industry to grow over time. We hope this is going to be short-lived although we cannot predict when it's going to be over," Roberson said.
The companies had announced on Aug. 4 that they were in merger talks.

The past year has been filled with difficulties for both companies. In addition to the fundamental industry troubles, Belmont chief executive Jerold Kennedy died in May of lung cancer and Cavalier founder and chief executive Jerry Wilson died of a heart attack in October.
